capabilities.notes: Synthetic account login, PHR bootstrap, consent acceptance, snapshot, proposal, and transition requests can traverse the public HTTP API.

The existing integration fixture writes synthetic source/evidence records through SessionLocal. A boundary adapter must declare this bootstrap exception and cannot attest evidence setup as an HTTP write.

Consent acceptance is public HTTP, but this endpoint has no consent-revocation operation. A revoked-consent schedule currently needs a separately designed isolated mutation boundary; it must not be represented as an all-HTTP schedule.
A synthetic proposal can reach the actual GLHS commitment persistence path through HTTP after authentication and scope/consent enforcement.
The commitment route does not expose a cache/index read or invalidation boundary. It cannot attest the required cache/index stage and is therefore unsuitable alone for headline RIVF execution.
Commitment-decision reconstruction exists, but a complete cross-boundary audit observer and a sanitized artifact contract still need implementation.

The four arm semantics have matching isolated service-local gate semantics. The gate requires explicit attestation, a clara-rivf-* project, a named arm, and non-production environment; absent configuration preserves strict behavior. No persistent HTTP adapter applies the arms yet, so none may return EXECUTED.

prohibited_attestations: A SessionLocal synthetic evidence fixture is an HTTP evidence writer.
A direct database consent mutation is a public HTTP governance mutation.
A research-arm config declaration is a faithful persistent-write implementation.
next_implementation_gate: Build an isolated-only adapter that combines a cache/index-bearing governed disclosure route with the HTTP persistent commit route, records each stage independently, and implements each arm without importing research configuration into production code.
